meta.method: Pass 1: news-first sweep of wet-season months (Apr–Nov) using Task 26 outlets and qualifying rule. Pass 2 (slimmed 2026-10-18): death queries with no site filter; Oyan Dam / Ogun River / lagoon / water-release / Isheri-Ajegunle-Owode-Agboyi queries; Anadolu once per year; out-of-season Jan–Mar and Dec. Qualifying reports name a Lagos State place and a date, and describe water on streets or in homes. Quotes ≤25 words, verbatim, and taken only from that report's own URL. Dates, numbers and quotes are only those in the source. Areas left as named; not geocoded. Flood date is the flood day, not publication day.
notes: Vanguard 11 Jul 2022 covers Friday 8 Jul (Egbe-Idimu / Mushin canal) and Saturday 9 Jul (Oko Oba / Oyatoki / Ipaja) on one URL; kept as r2022-003 on Friday 8 Jul for the confirmed Mushin canal death. Saturday scenes for that weekend come from other URLs.

NEMA 13 Jul wrap (Punch, Channels, Vanguard) attributes deaths to rainfall of 8–9 Jul. Punch and Channels say seven in Lagos; Vanguard's Farinloye quote splits five Lagos and two Ogun. Recorded as each outlet printed it.
Ogun Akute deaths and the Mile 2/Ojo boat capsize in the Vanguard weekend piece are not Lagos street/home flood fatalities.
Ugo (Egbe-Idimu) is missing, not confirmed dead, in Vanguard 11 Jul; Guardian 10 Jul states he was swept away to his death — deaths only on the Guardian report.
May 2022: Idumagbo stakeholder copy and building-collapse stories did not yield a dated street/home flood in Task 26 outlets.
August 2022: Cluster One / Garfa Street pieces are ongoing blockage or gully features, not a named flood day.
October Oyan Dam / Ogun River hits were relocate alerts. Punch 9 Nov is aftermath of 21 Oct, not a new day.
Anadolu 2022 copy was national (603 deaths) or 2023 Lagos; no 2022 Lagos flood day.
X accounts of LASEMA, Lagos MoE and NEMA: no dated 2022 flood posts reached.
Nairametrics, TVC and BBC Pidgin: no qualifying 2022 Lagos street/home flood day found (BBC Pidgin was the Third Mainland fact-check).

reports.impacts: Early-morning downpour yesterday hampered traffic for hours. Thunderstorm blew down billboards and road signs in Oregun; multiple crashes, no casualties per LASTMA. Motorists waded through flooded parts of Long and Otedola bridges; water on Otedola caused traffic to Berger.
reports.quote: motorists plying the Lagos- Ibadan Expressway had hectic time wading through flooded parts of the Long and Otedola bridges
reports.cause_quote: the two bridges have been retaining a large volume of water, any time it rains, thereby impeding free flow of traffic

reports.impacts: Saturday downpour lasting hours flooded roads and houses; property destroyed. Ketu-Ikosi roads to Mile 12 Market flooded; streets in Ikosi flooded; gridlock toward Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. Iya Beji: home in Alapere flooded through the back door. Victor: used a canoe to leave his house in Ikorodu. Lucy Ige stuck in traffic after floods blocked the road to Secretariat Bus Stop, Gbagada.
reports.quote: Roads and houses were flooded and property destroyed in Lagos on Saturday after a downpour which lasted for hours.
reports.cause_quote: urged the state government to work on coordinating their drainage channels and linking to avert perennial flooding

reports.impacts: Friday: commercial driver Ugo, 48, alias Gunners, washed into an open drainage on Yaya Hassan Street about 4 p.m.; not found dead or alive as of 7.30 p.m. Same Friday: 15-year-old Erinle Mouturayo Mary found dead in the Idi-Oro canal after slipping in on the way home from school. Saturday: man swept while searching for cows at Oko-Oba (outcome not stated); Lexus and another vehicle swept at Oyatoki, occupants later found alive. Saturday: more than 10 hours of rain overflowed Oko Oba Canal. Sunday: LASEMA rescued an elderly stroke patient trapped at Oluwaga, Ipaja. Mile 2/Ojo boat capsize in this piece is not logged as a street/home flood death.

reports.cause_quote: the overflowing of the Oko Oba Canal Channel which is presently undergoing expansion
reports.cause_who: Tunji Bello, Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources

Farinloye: three rescued alive, one jumped to safety, two missing at the 2.49 p.m. statement. Outcome of the two missing not stated in this report.

reports.impacts: Rain for days; Saturday: flooding and fare hikes. Agege Market wooden tables and chairs destroyed; wooden pedestrian bridge at the flyover destroyed. Lekki roads flooded; vehicles overwhelmed; people wading and some swimming in flood water. LASEMA: elderly woman with a stroke trapped in an Ipaja building after Saturday downpour, rescued alive. Farinloye: two vehicles swept at Orile-Agege; two occupants still missing, two persons feared dead.
reports.quote: In the Lekki area of Lagos, the roads were flooded, with vehicles overwhelmed by water.
reports.cause_quote: It is wrong for residents in the city to experience flood as a result of blocked drainage and gutters.

reports.impacts: LASEMA rescued an elderly woman trapped in her Ipaja-Ayobo building after Saturday's downpour. Near-drowning; she was alive but had a stroke. First aid then hospital. Flash flood ravaged parts of the state.
reports.quote: flooding had ravaged the area resorting to the near-drowning of the elderly woman
reports.cause_quote: trapped in her building as a result of flood occasioned by a downpour experienced in some parts of Lagos on Saturday

reports.impacts: Monday early-morning rain about four hours. Roads flooded: Marina, Pen Cinema, Aboru-Iyana-Ipaja-Ile-Epo, Dolphin Estate. Nine women rescued from a sinking building at 47 Akinwunmi Street, Mende; 35 buildings on Akinwumi Estate, 31 on Arowojobe, and Ebun Otti Estate impacted. Two men swept away and killed: Alfa returned to a flooded house; another missed his step on Command Bridge.

Two others with Alfa escaped. Nine ladies rescued from a one-storey building that started sinking on Akinwunmi Street; neighbouring houses displaced. Sylvester Diugwu: canal blocked by bamboo, water cannot reach the lagoon.

reports.impacts: Monday morning: storey building submerged after about four hours of rain, then started sinking. Nine female occupants rescued. Landlord escaped by ladder without alerting tenants; later questioned. Occupants Tosin Ademuyiwa and Blessing Uzokah had just renewed N300,000 annual rent and had nowhere to go. Rescue concluded about 11.56 a.m.; building cordoned for integrity testing.

reports.impacts: Yesterday: flood on Ibiwoye road and adjoining roads stranded commuters and shop owners. Motorists avoided the road; fares up about 50 percent. Chioma Enwerem: hard to leave home; water takes a week or more to dry. Victor Nwafada: stopped plying when it rains after flood damaged his tricycle last week.
reports.quote: floods that threw commuters, residents and shop owners into distress
reports.cause_quote: The flood was exacerbated by heavy rainfalls and blocked drainage systems that have defied solutions.

reports.impacts: Friday torrential rain overwhelmed buildings and washed away fences, including New Oko Oba. Jefferson Uwoghiren video from 2.30 p.m.: houses submerged, gates and fences washed away beside the canal. Dawodu: shoddy canal construction; same canal to Iyana-Ipaja, Command, Ayobo. LASEMA Oke-Osanyintolu: no casualty in New Oko Oba. Omotoso: flash flood, gone within hours after rain subsided.
reports.quote: houses are being submerged, gates and fences being removed and washed away by the flood
reports.cause_quote: the flood was caused by the shoddy construction of canals in the community
